messages:
jess: Heads-up: I'm rolling a small Terraform change to the Karpenter Provisioner nodeTemplate to add a taint for inference workloads (key=dedicated, value=inference:NoSchedule). Need quick sanity on how this interacts with HPA surge/eviction behavior. Also changing metrics-adapter secret path. TL;DR: will this cause transient pod evictions or HPA thrash?

mike: Can you paste the provisioner snippet + HPA config? mainly want to see tolerations and any stabilization settings (scaleUp/scaleDown).

jess: Provisioner snippet (from our TF plan):
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: prov-inference-canary
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
    operator: In
    values: [g5, a100]
  taints:
  - key: dedicated
    value: inference
    effect: NoSchedule
  labels:
    workload: inference-canary
```
and HPA we use for the inference deployment (excerpt):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics: ...
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
```
Also changing metrics adapter secret path from `kube-system/stackdriver-metrics` -> `infra/metrics-adapter-secret`.

samir: A few quick things:
- Adding `NoSchedule` to nodes will NOT evict existing pods. Only `NoExecute` evicts. So you're unlikely to cause immediate evictions.
- But new pods created by HPA that don't have the matching toleration will remain Pending -> HPA thinks pods aren't present and may scale more, causing "thrash".
- Karpenter consolidation might terminate nodes that become underutilized; if pods are Pending while nodes are removed that could make things worse.

anya: To expand: Karpenter will try to pack/shed nodes based on provisioner configuration. If you put the taint in the nodeTemplate, make sure pods you want on those nodes have the corresponding toleration + nodeSelector/affinity. Otherwise you either get Pending pods or unintended placement on expensive instances.

mike: On the metrics-adapter secret: update the adapter Deployment and the external metrics config. If the namespace/path changed, ensure RBAC + serviceaccount can read `infra/metrics-adapter-secret`. After deploy, check `kubectl describe deployment metrics-adapter -n infra` and `kubectl logs` if HPA shows `failed to get external metric`.

jess: Good catch. My plan: create a canary provisioner `prov-inference-canary` with taint+label, roll a canary deployment of the inference service with toleration and nodeSelector `workload: inference-canary`. Also update metrics-adapter secret in infra namespace and point HPA external metric to the new namespace. Will run in staging first.

mike: Recommend adding toleration like:
```yaml
tolerations:
- key: dedicated
  operator: Equal
  value: inference
  effect: NoSchedule
```
And test by scaling manually to ensure pods land. Also bump `behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 60s for the canary to reduce spike reaction.

samir: Alternative (safer): don't taint all inference nodes at once. Create the canary provisioner with `limits: { resources: { cpu: "1000m" } }` or smaller capacity so only a subset of traffic gets scheduled there. That reduces blast radius. Also add a short pre-stop hook to the inference pods so termination is graceful.

anya: FYI VPA + HPA: VPA in "recommendation" mode is fine, but if you try Vertical updates with HPA-managed pods you'll run into issues. For inference bursts VPA is less useful; prefer buffer nodes or autoscaler tuning.

infra-bot: terraform plan for `prov-inference-canary` completed in staging: https://ci.internal/reports/plan/2431122334 (plan shows taint + node label only) :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: reminder: after you apply, run `kubectl get pods -n staging -o wide | grep inference` and `kubectl get hpa -n staging` then `kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>` if any Pending.

jess: Plan to: 1) apply canary provisioner in staging 2) deploy canary inferred service with toleration + nodeSelector 3) update metrics-adapter secret path in infra 4) set HPA scaleUp stabilization to 60s and keep scaleDown at 300s 5) monitor Pending pods and HPA events. Will also add a Prom alert for Pending>5m.

mike: LGTM :thumbsup: I'll watch staging for Pending pods and check events. If you want I can attach to a `kubectl describe` when you see one.

samir: Don't forget to add the secret path change to the terraform state migration notes and run `terraform state mv` if needed. Also update our runbook.

anya: Add a quick docs blurb in infra runbook about "tainting canary provisioner" + expected behavior so oncall isn't surprised. :sparkles:

jess: Thanks all — I'll kick this off in ~30m and post results here.
